label: Human Figure (generic)
appearance: Upright human form in period dress or nude; typically rendered with cross-hatched drapery, fine line work for anatomy, and ground-shadow in early modern copperplate style.
description: The generic human figure in emblem imagery is the operator, observer, or subject of the alchemical drama. Clothed figures denote social roles (philosopher, artisan, noble); nude figures indicate the prima materia or the purified soul stripped of accident.

label: Warrior / Knight / Soldier
appearance: Armoured or partially armoured male figure carrying weapon; plate armour, halberd, sword, or pike; often shown in dynamic posture.
description: The warrior in alchemical emblems figures the coagulating or fixing principle — the force that subdues volatile matter. Associated with Mars, the combative stage of fixation, and heroic descent myths (Perseus, Hercules).

label: Angel / Winged Messenger
appearance: Winged humanoid figure, usually in flowing robes; wings are large and feathered; often depicted descending from a cloud or bearing an object (trumpet, scroll, vessel).
description: Angels in alchemical emblems mediate between the celestial and terrestrial operations. They announce stage transitions, carry the divine fire (Prometheus motif), and in Rosicrucian emblems (Cramer, Fludd) serve as agents of divine wisdom.

label: King / Sol / Rex
appearance: Male figure with crown and sceptre, robes; in Maier often depicted with the sun disc; typically shown seated on throne or standing in regal posture with rich cross-hatched drapery.
description: The solar, sulphurous, masculine principle. The king must die (mortificatio) and be resurrected; his body becomes the red tincture. In conjunction with the queen he enacts the coniunctio oppositorum.

label: Queen / Luna / Regina
appearance: Female figure with crown or lunar crescent; robes, often white or shown against the moon; in Rosarium Philosophorum depicted as bride receiving the king in the bath.
description: The lunar, mercurial, feminine principle. As bride she receives the king's death; as resurrected queen she embodies the albedo and the white tincture. In Maier she is Atalanta, the fleet-footed silver.

label: Hermaphrodite / Androgyne / Rebis
appearance: A single body bearing attributes of both sexes: one breast exposed, dual clothing, sun and moon crowns, or the two-headed Rebis figure standing on a winged dragon or sphere; often flanked by Sol and Luna.
description: The coniunctio made visible: a single body bearing the attributes of sun and moon, king and queen, red and white. The Rebis is the completed Stone. Central to Rosarium, Maier emblem 33, and Khunrath's Amphitheatrum.

label: Philosopher / Old Man / Sage / Hermit
appearance: Aged bearded male in long robes, often carrying staff, book, or lantern; in workshop or landscape setting; sometimes hooded or cloaked. Witch variants are elderly female figures with attributes of cauldron or broom.
description: The contemplative figure of the adept or philosopher: he who reads nature rather than acting on it. In emblems he often appears beside the furnace, reading the stars, or receiving divine revelation. The crone or witch (in Maier emblem 5) is a dark inversion — the nursing or seducing aspect of the feminine prima materia.

label: Child / Infant / Putto
appearance: Infant or young child figure; in alchemical contexts often naked (filius philosophorum), held or nursed; in decorative contexts as flying putti in the borders of emblem plates.
description: The child in alchemical emblems is the filius philosophorum, the Stone newly born from the union of king and queen. In Maier emblems 1-2 the infant is nurtured by the Earth (prima materia). The nursing of the infant is an emblem for the patient ripening of the Work.

label: Skeleton / Death Figure
appearance: Articulated human skeleton, often carrying scythe or hourglass; may be dancing, enthroned, or lying prostrate; rendered in fine line-work showing each bone.
description: The skeleton figures mortificatio, the death of metals or the dissolution of the body prior to resurrection. Death is a necessary stage in the Work: the king must die before he can be resurrected as the philosophical gold. Found prominently in Atalanta Fugiens emblems 6, 8, and 32.

label: Dragon / Wyvern / Winged Serpent
appearance: Winged reptilian creature with four or two legs; in early modern engravings rendered with cross-hatched scales and large spread wings; often coiled or rampant; sometimes two dragons fighting or devouring each other.
description: Winged or wingless reptilian creature; the volatile mercury, the prima materia before fixation, or the guardian of the threshold. The ouroboros (self-devouring serpent) is a specialised form. In Maier, two dragons fight (sulphur vs mercury) in emblem 16.

label: Lion
appearance: Rampant or passant leonine figure with large mane; in early modern prints the mane is rendered with dense radial hatching; tail curled upward; may be shown devouring a sun disc (green lion) or coloured red (red lion) in illuminated versions.
description: The green lion (vitriol) devours the sun (gold); the red lion is the perfected sulphur. Lions also appear as royal, solar beasts in heraldic and triumphalist contexts. Central to Maier emblems 16 (green lion) and 24.

label: Serpent / Snake / Caduceus
appearance: Legless reptile, sinuous body; in caduceus form two serpents wound about a staff; as ouroboros a single serpent biting its own tail in a circle; scale patterns rendered with fine cross-hatching.
description: Distinguished from the winged dragon: the serpent without wings is the fixed mercury or the Hermetic caduceus. The ouroboros (emblem 14 in Maier) represents cyclic self-completion and the unity of beginning and end. The bitten serpent (Nehushtan) represents purified poison.

label: Bird (generic) / Eagle
appearance: Large winged bird, often shown in flight or perched on a branch or rock; eagle rendered with spread wings and hooked beak; smaller birds in landscape settings shown in silhouette.
description: The eagle represents sublimation and the ascent of volatile spirit. As alchemical volatile principle, it contrasts with the lion (fixed). In Maier emblem 44 the eagle carries a stone to the sun; in emblem 50 the king is raised by birds.

label: Phoenix
appearance: Eagle-like bird in or rising from flames; in early modern prints shown with spread wings and rays emanating, often perched on a pyre of burning wood.
description: The phoenix is the supreme emblem of the rubedo: the resurrection of the perfected Stone from the ashes of the mortificatio. It is the completion of the nigredo-albedo-rubedo cycle, proof that dissolution and death lead to a higher life.

label: Pelican (Feeding its Young)
appearance: Large white waterbird with distinctive pouch; in alchemical/emblematic convention shown piercing its own breast to feed young with its blood; rendered with broad wing-spread and chicks in nest below.
description: The pelican in her piety (pelicanus in pietate) is the emblem of the philosopher's Stone nourishing and perfecting lesser metals with its own tincture. Also figures Christ's sacrifice, making this a central Rosicrucian emblem.

label: Raven / Crow (Nigredo Bird)
appearance: Entirely black bird, rendered in solid ink or dense cross-hatching; typically perched on a rock, skull, or the corpse of the king; beak open.
description: The raven or crow (corvus niger) is the bird of the nigredo: the blackening of matter in the first stage of the Work. The head of the raven (caput corvi) is a standard emblem for putrefaction. In Maier, the raven appears as a herald of dissolution.

label: Dove / White Bird
appearance: Small white bird in flight or perched; rendered with fine feather hatching; often shown descending from above or nesting in a branch.
description: The dove figures the albedo: the whitening of matter after the nigredo. As Holy Spirit (Spiritus Sanctus) in Rosicrucian emblems, it descends to animate the newly purified matter. The dove of Venus also signals the emergence of love and harmony from the coniunctio.

label: Peacock (Cauda Pavonis)
appearance: Large bird with spectacular spread tail showing eye-patterns; the many-coloured tail is the defining visual; rendered in engraving with repeated eye-spot patterns though rarely in colour in print editions.
description: The peacock's tail (cauda pavonis) marks the citrinitas: the stage of many colours that appears between the albedo and rubedo, signalling that all the colours of the spectrum are present before the final reddening. A moment of near-completion.

label: Swan
appearance: Large white waterbird with long curved neck; shown on water or in flight; entirely white plumage rendered with fine parallel lines or left white against hatched background.
description: The white swan is an albedo emblem: the whitened, purified matter that floats on the mercurial water. The swan's song (canto cygni) is the last sigh of the Work at the point of completion, and its pure whiteness emblems the perfected silver tincture.

label: Horse / Steed
appearance: Equine figure, often in motion (galloping, rearing); in classical emblems may be winged (Pegasus); rendered with cross-hatched musculature; frequently shown bearing a rider or running free.
description: The horse in alchemical emblems figures the volatile, passionate, or unstable principle that the adept must tame (fixation). Pegasus links to inspiration and sublimation. The rearing horse also appears as an emblem of uncontrolled sulphur requiring the water of mercury to restrain it.

label: Dog / Hound
appearance: Domesticated canine; greyhound type (lean, long-legged) or mastiff (heavy, square-muzzled); often shown beside a figure or in pursuit.
description: The dog in alchemical and emblematic imagery figures fidelity, the companion of the adept, or — in its devouring form — the dissolution of the body. The dog eating cadavers was a standard emblem of the nigredo. In Maier emblem 42 the dog and wolf devour the dead man.

label: Wolf
appearance: Wild canine with heavy fur and open jaws; rendered with dense hatching for thick pelt; shown in threatening posture or devouring something.
description: The wolf is antimony (lupus metallorum) in alchemical tradition: it devours the king (gold) in order to purify it. This devoration removes base metal contamination. The wolf of antimony is a central motif in Maier and Flamel. Also used as emblem of rapacity and ungoverned appetite.

label: Deer / Stag / Hart
appearance: Graceful cervine figure with branching antlers (stag) or without (hind); shown in landscape setting, often fleeing or drinking from a stream.
description: The stag appears in alchemical emblems as the swift, fleeing spirit or the sacred quarry of the hunt (Actaeon motif). Its shedding of antlers connects to cyclical renewal. In Maier emblem 0, Atalanta is sometimes paired with the deer as emblem of the fleeing first matter.

label: Ox / Bull / Taurus
appearance: Large bovine figure with heavy body and short horns (ox) or long curved horns (bull); shown plowing or standing in landscape; dense hatching for thick hide.
description: The ox figures the fixed, earthly, patient laboring principle. As Taurus, it governs the earth element and the stabilizing fixation of mercury. In Maier emblem 6 ('sow gold in white earth') the agricultural setting implies the ox as the engine of the opus.

label: Lamb / Agnus Dei
appearance: Small woolly ovine figure, often shown kneeling or recumbent; in devotional contexts may carry a cross-staff (Agnus Dei); rendered with dense curly hatching for fleece.
description: The sacrificial lamb (Agnus Dei) in Rosicrucian emblems connects the alchemical sacrifice to Christian atonement. In secular emblematic tradition the lamb also figures gentleness, purity, and the first matter before transformation.

label: Fish / Pisces
appearance: Aquatic creature with scales, fins, and tail; may be shown in water, in a net, or being caught; scale patterns rendered with overlapping arcs; sometimes two fish facing opposite directions (Pisces).
description: Fish in alchemical imagery live in the mercurial water and represent the dissolved metals or the prima materia floating in the philosophical sea. To fish for the Stone is a standard emblem of the extraction of gold from the primordial waters.

label: Tortoise / Turtle
appearance: Low-slung reptile with domed hexagonal-patterned shell; shown in profile with legs and head extended; shell pattern is a distinctive visual marker in engravings.
description: The tortoise emblematizes slowness, patience, and the long duration of the alchemical Work (festina lente — hasten slowly). It also figures the primordial earth as world-support in cosmological emblems. Appears in Hypnerotomachia Polyphili as Fortuna's attribute.

label: Crab / Cancer
appearance: Crustacean with pincer claws and segmented carapace; shown frontally or in profile; claws are the visually dominant element; rendered with precise line work showing shell segments.
description: The crab (Cancer) governs the summer solstice and the turning point of the year. In alchemical emblems it figures the retrograde motion of the Work, the backwards step in maturation, or the moment when the matter 'moves sideways' rather than progressing. Also an attribute of the moon and the zodiacal sign of Cancer.

label: Bee / Apis
appearance: Small striped insect with wings; typically shown near flowers or a hive; wings translucent and rendered with fine parallel lines; often shown in swarm.
description: Bees figure industry, wisdom, and the generation of the philosophers' honey (the tincture). The beehive is the opus in miniature: the sealed vessel in which countless operations produce the sweet gold. In Maier, the bee's generation without sexual congress emblems the virgin birth of the Stone.

label: Butterfly / Psyche
appearance: Winged insect with symmetrical patterned wings; shown in flight or resting on flower; wings rendered with detailed vein patterns and symmetrical markings.
description: The butterfly is the immortal soul (psyche) emerging from the chrysalis (putrefaction). Its metamorphosis from caterpillar through death-like pupa to winged creature perfectly emblematizes the nigredo-albedo-rubedo sequence. The butterfly with a flame means the soul consumed by divine love.

label: Fox / Vulpes
appearance: Slim reddish-brown canine with pointed muzzle and bushy tail; typically shown in sly posture, often near a chicken coop or grape vine.
description: The fox in emblematic tradition figures cunning, deception, and the principle that deceives even the wise (the fallacy of appearances). In alchemical context, the fox destroying the vineyard (Song of Songs) represents the corrosive acids or the putrefaction that destroys the visible form to reveal the hidden tincture.

label: Hare / Rabbit
appearance: Long-eared leaping animal; rendered with dense body hatching and prominent long ears; shown in running or leaping posture.
description: The hare is a lunar animal, sacred to Diana/Hecate, and a figure of the fleeting, elusive prima materia. In Maier's frontispiece Atalanta runs, and the hare's speed emblematizes the volatile first matter that the adept must catch before it escapes.

label: Bear / Ursus
appearance: Massive shaggy quadruped with small round ears; shown upright or on all fours; dense cross-hatching for thick pelt.
description: The bear in emblematic tradition figures raw power, the unformed, and the primitive stage. The she-bear licking her cubs into shape emblematizes the sculptor's or adept's work of giving form to the formless prima materia. Ursus is also associated with the north and Saturn.

label: Tree / Arbor Philosophica
appearance: Upright woody plant with branching crown; in emblematic prints often stylized with perfectly balanced branching; may bear sun and moon as fruit; roots shown exposed or entering earth.
description: The philosophical tree (arbor philosophica) grows from the putrefied seed of the Stone. Bears sun and moon as fruit; may be a rose tree (Rosarium) or a golden tree (Aureum Vellus). In Maier emblem 4 a king and queen grow from the same root.

label: Rose / Rosa Philosophica
appearance: Stylized five-petalled flower on thorny stem; in early modern engravings rendered with concentric petal lines and visible thorns; roses grow in gardens, on bushes, or are held by figures.
description: The rose is the emblem of the philosophical secret (sub rosa), the tincture, and the coniunctio. The red rose is the sulphurous rubedo tincture; the white rose the mercurial albedo. The garden of roses (rosarium) is the space of the coniunctio. Title emblem of the Rosarium Philosophorum.

label: Lily / Lilium
appearance: Tall-stemmed flower with large trumpet-shaped petals; usually white; rendered with smooth curved petal lines contrasting with hatched stem; may appear in vases or garden settings.
description: The white lily emblematizes purity, the albedo, and the Virgin (Maria). In alchemical emblems it grows in the garden where the coniunctio is performed and represents the perfected white tincture before reddening. The lily and rose together = albedo and rubedo complete.

label: Thistle / Spina
appearance: Spiky-leaved plant with round purple flower head; prominent sharp spines on leaves and stem; rendered with starburst flower head and jagged leaf edges.
description: The thistle and thorn in emblems figure pain, the sharp trial, and the obstacle that guards the treasure. The philosopher must pass through the thorns to reach the rose. In agricultural emblems thorns and thistles are the weeds of unworked earth — the prima materia in its crude state.

label: Vine / Grape / Vitis
appearance: Climbing plant with large lobed leaves and hanging clusters of round grapes; often shown trained on a trellis or winding about a tree; grapes rendered as clusters of small circles.
description: The vine and grape emblem the fermentation and distillation process (vinification = sublimation). Dionysus/Bacchus as patron of the vine connects the intoxication of wine to the illumination of the tincture. 'The foxes that spoil the vines' (Song of Songs) = corrosive acids destroying the body to liberate the spirit.

label: Flower / Herb (generic)
appearance: Generic botanical element: small flowering plants in foreground, grasses in landscape, reeds at water's edge, palm tree silhouette; all rendered in simple line-work as landscape fill.
description: Generic plant life in emblems signals the garden of nature (natura naturans), the growing principle, and the earth's generative power. Medicinal herbs signal the healing and purifying aspect of the Work; reeds and grasses the liminal zones of water and earth.

label: Wreath / Laurel / Crown of Leaves
appearance: Circular garland of leaves, either worn on the head or depicted as a decorative framing device; laurel has small oval pointed leaves; may also be worn by personifications of Victory.
description: The laurel wreath is the emblem of Apollo (Sol), victory, and immortality. In alchemical emblems, crowning a figure with laurel signals completion of a stage or the triumph of the tincture. Oak wreaths signal the earthly completion of the Stoic philosopher.

label: Oak / Robur
appearance: Stout-trunked tree with deeply lobed leaves and pendant acorns; heavily branched; bark rendered with vertical fissure lines; broader than tall with spreading crown.
description: The oak is Jupiter's tree, emblem of strength, durability, and the earth's solidity. In Rosicrucian emblems the oak forest is the forest of initiation (the Brothers of the Rosy Cross met in such a forest). The acorn-to-oak cycle is used as an emblem of the slow maturation of the Stone.

label: Mountain / Cave / Rocky Ground
appearance: Ranges from craggy peaks with hatched rock faces to gentle rolling hills; cave openings rendered as dark ellipses with radiating shadow hatching; foreground rocks as roughly triangular forms with parallel weathering lines.
description: The mountain is both prima materia (the raw earth) and the destination of VITRIOL: Visita Interiora Terrae Rectificando Invenies Occultum Lapidem. Grottos are thresholds between surface and interior work. In Maier, the mountain is the laboratory of Nature herself.

label: Fountain / Spring / Stream
appearance: Architectural fountain with basin and central jet; or natural spring emerging from rock; water rendered with parallel curved lines or stippling; the bath (balneum) is a rectangular vessel filled with water.
description: The mercurial fountain, the philosophical water, the bath of purification. The mercurial spring dissolves and purifies; the bain-marie (Maria's bath) gently heats. In Maier emblem 9 the philosopher bathes in the mercurial spring to achieve whitening.

label: Sun / Sol / Solar Disc
appearance: Circular disc with radiating rays, either straight or wavy; in early modern prints rays alternate long-short; often shown in the upper portion of plates; may have a face (personified sun).
description: The solar disc, radiate crown, or personified Sol. Governs gold, fire, and the masculine principle throughout the alchemical tradition. In conjunction with the moon, the coniunctio produces the hermaphrodite and the Stone.

label: Moon / Luna / Crescent
appearance: Crescent form (horns pointing left or right) or full disc; often shown in upper corners of emblem plates opposite the sun; may have a face; stars may surround it.
description: The lunar crescent or personified Luna. Governs silver, water, and the feminine principle. In conjunction with the sun the coniunctio produces the hermaphrodite. Luna also governs the tidal, cyclical, and dreaming aspects of the Work.

label: Star / Celestial Body / Zodiac
appearance: Five or six-pointed stars; shown in groups against dark hatched sky; may be arranged in zodiacal patterns; the morning star (Venus) sometimes shown as a particularly bright point.
description: Celestial bodies govern alchemical timing and correspondence. Stars, planetary symbols, and zodiacal figures mark the macrocosmic scaffold that the Work mirrors below. The seven planets are the seven metals; the stars are the influences raining down on the Work.

label: Fire / Flame
appearance: Upward-pointing tongues of flame with curling tips; rendered with fine curves; lighter at the base (yellow region), darker at tips (orange-red); may surround a figure, rise from a bowl, or consume a pyre.
description: Fire is the prime mover of all alchemical operations. Too much destroys; calibrated fire transforms. The philosophical fire (ignis philosophicus) is not ordinary fire but the patient, graduated heat of the athanor. In emblems, fire also figures passion, purification by burning, and divine illumination.

label: Water / River / Sea
appearance: Flowing water rendered with parallel horizontal wavy lines; still pools with gentle ripple lines; ocean with larger wave forms; rivers shown between banks with prominent flow-lines.
description: Water in alchemical emblems is the mercurial solvent: the philosophical water (aqua mercurialis) dissolves all metals. The sea (mare philosophicum) is the totality of dissolved matter before form returns. Water also figures the prima materia in its liquid, undifferentiated state.

label: Cloud / Sky / Atmosphere
appearance: Billowing cumulus forms rendered with curved outlines and internal arc-hatching; sky shown as a receding upper zone with lighter hatching; vapour or mist as thin wispy horizontals.
description: Clouds in alchemical emblems figure volatility and sublimation: the vapours rising from the heated vessel. The cloud is the medium of the spirit between heaven and earth, and in emblems divine presences or messages descend from cloud banks. The volatile spirit of the metal rises as cloud before it is fixed.

label: Earth / Ground / Forest / Soil
appearance: Earth shown as hatched ground plane with grass tufts; forest as silhouetted trees in distance; volcanic mountains with plume at peak; soil as darkly hatched terrain.
description: The Earth (terra) is one of the four elements and the nurse of the Stone (emblem 1: Nutrix ejus terra est). The philosopher's earth is the fixed, receiving matter; the forest is the wild, uninitiated nature prior to cultivation. Volcanic earth signals subterranean fire and the union of fire with earth.

label: Rainbow / Iris
appearance: Arched bands of colour spanning the sky; in black-and-white prints rendered as parallel arcs of varying width; may span from horizon to horizon or emerge from a cloud.
description: The rainbow (iris) signals the cauda pavonis in the heavens: all colours present as a divine covenant. After the deluge of nigredo, the rainbow promises completion. In Khunrath's Amphitheatrum the rainbow appears as a sign of divine presence over the alchemical work.

label: Lightning / Thunderbolt / Fulgur
appearance: Jagged zigzag stroke descending from a cloud; often shown with secondary branches; rendered as a bright gap in otherwise hatched sky.
description: The thunderbolt (fulgur Jovis) is divine fire descending from the heavens: sudden illumination, divine election, or the calcination that strikes the Work from without. In Fludd and Khunrath the lightning is the divine Light that initiates the adept.

label: Furnace / Athanor / Hearth
appearance: Domed or cylindrical tower-shaped furnace (athanor) with fire door at base and ash-pit below; in engravings rendered as a chimney-tower with visible fire at the opening; workshop hearth is a low open fireplace.
description: The source of alchemical heat: athanor, open furnace, or allegorical fire. Governs the timing of every stage; too much fire destroys the work. The athanor (from Arabic al-tannur, the bread oven) provides gentle sustained heat. Appears prominently in Maier, Mylius, and Khunrath laboratory scenes.

label: Castle / Tower / Fortification
appearance: Stone-built structure with crenellated battlements; towers shown as cylindrical or square pillars with arrow-slit windows; ruins with collapsed sections; domestic buildings with pitched roofs and small windows.
description: The castle or tower in emblems is the sealed vessel writ large: the philosophical fortress that contains and defends the Work. It is also the philosopher's tower of contemplation (ivory tower), and in mythological emblems the tower of Danaë (gold raining down = rubedo). Ruins signal the decay and mortificatio necessary before rebuilding.

label: Temple / Altar / Sacred Space
appearance: Classical temple with columns and pediment, or gothic church with pointed arches; altar as a simple stone table with offerings; interior sacred spaces shown in perspective with vaulted ceilings.
description: The temple is the sacred space in which the alchemical Work takes place — it is both the laboratory and the oratory (Khunrath's Amphitheatrum shows both side by side). The altar is where the sacrifice (mortificatio) is performed and the offering is made to the divine fire.

label: Bridge / Transitus
appearance: Arched stone bridge spanning a river or chasm; in early modern prints rendered with semicircular arches and keystones; may be shown with figures crossing.
description: The bridge is the emblem of transition between stages: the narrow passage from one state of matter to another. In emblematic tradition it is the pons philosophorum connecting the terrestrial and celestial realms, and the rite of passage that the adept must cross.

label: Labyrinth / Maze
appearance: Concentric spiral or rectangular-turn maze; shown as a flat ground plan or architectural structure; paths rendered as alternating light and dark bands.
description: The labyrinth is the emblem of the complex, winding path of the alchemical Work and of initiation. The Theseus-Minotaur myth maps onto the adept entering the darkness of the prima materia (the Minotaur = the monstrous first matter) and finding the hidden centre (the Stone). Maier emblem 38 directly engages the labyrinth.

label: Gate / Arch / Column
appearance: Triumphal arch with columns and decorated keystone; gate as a pair of heavy doors in a stone frame; column as a free-standing pillar on a base with capital; all rendered in classical architectural vocabulary.
description: The gate and arch figure initiation thresholds: the point of no return where the adept passes from the profane to the sacred sphere of the Work. Columns (the pillars of Hercules) mark the boundary of the known world. The gate through which the philosopher passes is the entrance to the inner sanctum of nature.

label: Tomb / Monument / Obelisk / Sepulchre
appearance: Stone sarcophagus or chest on a plinth; obelisk as tall tapering square pillar; pyramid as triangle form; all rendered in massive stone with simple classical decoration.
description: The tomb is the vessel of mortificatio: the sealed space where the king's body putrefies before resurrection. It is both the sepulchre of the Work and the womb of the new Stone. The obelisk marks the solar principle in its most durable, mineralized form — the solidified ray of the sun.

label: Vessel / Philosophical Egg / Flask
appearance: Round-bellied glass or clay container with narrow neck; alembic has a domed cap with condensation tube; retort is a pear-shaped flask with long curved neck; the philosophical egg is oval and sealed; rendered with smooth outlines and light hatching to suggest translucency.
description: The sealed container in which the Work proceeds: glass flask, clay vessel, philosophical egg (ovum philosophicum), alembic, or retort. The vessel is the microcosmic world in which the opus is performed. It must be sealed hermetically to prevent the volatile spirit from escaping.

label: Crucible / Melting Pot
appearance: Open-topped ceramic cup on a trivet over fire; typically conical or hemispherical; shown with molten material visible inside; often held with tongs.
description: The crucible (unlike the sealed flask) is the open vessel for calcinatio and fusion: the space of extreme heat, dissolution of form, and the reduction of metal to its simplest state. It figures the moment of total surrender before the new form is poured.

label: Sword / Gladius
appearance: Double-edged straight blade with cross-guard and grip; rendered with fine parallel lines on the blade to suggest steel; may be drawn and held aloft or sheathed at a figure's side.
description: The sword in alchemical emblems is the instrument of discrimination: it separates the pure from the impure, the fixed from the volatile. The sword of Mercury (gladius mercurialis) cuts through appearances. In Rosicrucian emblems the two-edged sword is divine judgment. The angel's flaming sword guards the secret of the Stone.

label: Spear / Lance / Javelin
appearance: Long pole with pointed metal tip; in early modern prints rendered as a slender vertical line with a triangular or leaf-shaped head; may be carried at rest or in throwing posture.
description: The lance and spear figure penetration and the perforation of the sealed matter: the operation of coagulation that fixes the volatile spirit. The spear of Longinus (the Holy Lance) in Rosicrucian emblems pierces the king's side to draw the tincturing blood.

label: Shield / Clypeus
appearance: Flat defensive surface, either round (buckler) or kite-shaped (heraldic); often bearing a blazon or device; rendered in profile or at a three-quarter angle showing the boss or grip.
description: The shield figures defense, the containing wall of the Work, and in heraldic contexts the identity and lineage of the figure bearing it. The Medusa-shield (aegis) turns the gaze of matter back on itself — a figure for the mirroring self-knowledge that unlocks the Stone.

label: Staff / Wand / Caduceus
appearance: Simple wooden staff (walking stick length); wand as shorter, thinner; caduceus as staff with two serpents wound about it and wings at top; thyrsus topped with pine cone; all vertical held objects in figures' hands.
description: The staff is the authority of the adept and the instrument of his work. The caduceus (Mercury's staff with two serpents) is the supreme alchemical instrument: the binding together of opposites (the two serpents = sulphur and mercury) that produces the tincture. The thyrsus of Dionysus signals ecstatic dissolution.

label: Sceptre / Royal Staff / Orb-and-Sceptre
appearance: Short ornate staff topped with a globe, fleur-de-lis, or cross; held by royal or divine figures; rendered with elaborate top ornament on a straight shaft.
description: The sceptre is the emblem of royal authority and the philosopher's sovereignty over matter. In the hand of the alchemical king it signals his dominion over the four elements. The orb and sceptre together signal complete dominion: the globe of matter under the royal power of Art.

label: Key / Clavis
appearance: Traditional key with bow (circular grip), stem (shaft), and bit (teeth); golden keys may be elaborately decorated; shown in a figure's hand, hung from a belt, or in a lock.
description: The key is one of the most pregnant alchemical symbols: the clavis opens the sealed vessel and unlocks the secret of the Stone. The twelve keys of Basil Valentine enumerate twelve operations; in Rosicrucian emblems the key unlocks the Castle of Wisdom. The key also figures gnosis: the knowledge that opens nature.

label: Chain / Rope / Binding
appearance: Linked metal chain or twisted rope; shown binding a figure's wrists or ankles, or as a festoon between objects; individual links rendered as ovals with visible connection points.
description: The chain in emblems figures the binding of one principle to another: fixation, the subjugation of the volatile to the fixed. Prometheus' chain represents the fixing of divine fire to matter. The golden chain (aurea catena Homeri) links all levels of being from heaven to earth and is the structure of correspondence itself.

label: Crown / Corona
appearance: Royal corona with points or arches; shown on heads of king/queen figures or held aloft; golden crowns rendered with elaborate fleur-de-lis points and gem settings.
description: The crown as a standalone object (detached from the figure wearing it) signals the prize: the completed Stone is crowned, as the king is crowned at his restoration. In Maier, the crowning of the philosophical child is an emblem of the Stone's completion. The crown falling from the king's head emblematizes mortificatio.

label: Ring / Annulus / Circle
appearance: Circular band; finger rings shown in profile or on a hand; decorative rings may bear a gemstone; the signet ring has a flat seal face.
description: The ring is the emblem of cyclic completion, the perfect circle, and the sealed bond. The ring of Saturn (Saturnus) binds and limits. The wedding ring (annulus coniugalis) is the emblem of the sacred marriage. The ouroboros as ring is the most condensed alchemical symbol: the cycle of dissolution and coagulation made circular.

label: Book / Scroll / Codex
appearance: Closed or open book with visible pages; scroll as rolled parchment with visible text; in early modern prints books have elaborate tooled leather bindings; open books show text columns with decorative initials.
description: The book in alchemical emblems is the Liber naturae: the book of nature that the adept reads instead of paper. It also figures the revealed scripture (Hermes Trismegistus' Emerald Tablet, the Rosicrucian manifestos). The philosopher reading a book embodies the studious contemplative phase of the Work.

label: Torch / Lamp / Candle
appearance: Torch as a wooden handle with flaming head; lamp as an oil vessel with wick and small flame; candle as a wax cylinder with a bright tip; lantern as a glass-enclosed lamp; all shown with a small defined flame.
description: The torch and lamp figure the philosophical light that illuminates the darkness of the prima materia. Prometheus' torch is the divine fire of Art. In Rosicrucian emblems the lamp carried by the Brother lights the dark forest of initiation. Heraclitus' logos is a torch passed through the darkness of generation.

label: Mirror / Speculum
appearance: Circular or oval polished surface in an ornate frame; handled mirrors shown as disc on a long stem; may reflect a figure or scene; rendered with a bright blank oval representing the reflective surface.
description: The mirror is the emblem of self-knowledge (gnothi seauton) and the mirroring of the macrocosm in the microcosm. Nature looks at herself in the alchemist's mirror; the philosopher sees in it not himself but the prima materia as it truly is. Prudence holds a mirror to see future consequences; Vanity holds it to see only herself.

label: Hourglass / Sandglass / Tempus
appearance: Two glass bulbs connected at a narrow waist, mounted in a wooden frame; sand visible falling through the neck; held by Death (skeleton) or placed on a table.
description: The hourglass figures the precise timing of the alchemical Work and the limitation of the operator's time. The Work must be completed before the sands run out. Saturn holds the hourglass as Tempus (Time): the great enemy of the opus who destroys matter through age if the adept is not swift enough.

label: Scales / Balance / Libra
appearance: Two-pan beam balance on a central pivot; shown with equal or unequal pans; justice's scales have a sword paired with them; analytical scales have a pointer at the centre of the beam.
description: The scales figure justice, proportion, and the precise weighing of materials that the alchemist must perform. In emblematic tradition, the balance of opposites (hot/cold, wet/dry, sol/luna) is the precondition of the coniunctio. Too much of one quality destroys the proportion of the Work.

label: Globe / Sphere / Orb
appearance: Circular sphere on a stand; terrestrial globe shows landmasses; celestial globe shows constellation lines; orb is a plain sphere topped with a cross; all rendered as perfect circles with hatching to suggest roundness.
description: The sphere is the most perfect geometric form and emblem of the completed, unified Work. The globe of the world (sphaera mundi) is the macrocosm that the Work mirrors. In Maier, the philosopher surrounds the circular system of the Work with square, triangle, and circle (emblem 21), and the sphere is the unitary resolution of all opposites.

label: Wheel / Rota / Bellows
appearance: Spoked wheel in full profile; Fortune's wheel has figures clinging to its rim at various heights; the rota philosophorum has text on the rim; bellows are wedge-shaped with a long nozzle.
description: The wheel (rota Fortunae) figures the cyclical nature of all things, including the alchemical stages. What rises must fall and rise again. The rota philosophorum shows the sequence of operations. Bellows supply the philosophical fire: they are the operator's instrument for calibrating heat and keeping the Work alive.

label: Axe / Hammer / Scythe
appearance: Axe with broad curved blade on a wooden handle; hammer with square iron head; scythe with long curved blade and long handle; all tools of cutting, shaping, and harvesting.
description: The axe and hammer figure the initial labors of the Work: breaking down, dividing, and separating. Saturn's scythe harvests the crop of the Work at the appointed time. The hammer of Vulcan shapes the raw metal on the anvil of matter. These are the instruments of the first, violent stages of the opus.

label: Musical Instrument (Lute / Trumpet / Drum)
appearance: Lute as a pear-shaped body with frets and tuning pegs; trumpet as a long or coiled brass tube with bell; drum as a cylindrical body with skin heads; shown being played by figures or placed as attributes.
description: Musical instruments in alchemical emblems invoke the Pythagorean harmony of the spheres that governs the proportions of the Work. Maier's Atalanta Fugiens is itself a musical work: each emblem has a fugue. The trumpet announces stage transitions and divine presence; the drum marks the martial time of fixation.
